title: HLA-B27, CD21, the Reverse Syphilis Algorithm and Assay Limits
summary: Learn why HLA-B27 marks risk rather than ankylosing spondylitis, why EBV infects B cells through CD21, how to read the reverse syphilis algorithm and its discordant result, and why anti-dsDNA platforms and blood cytokine levels can disagree or mislead.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 44 Hits 11 (HLA-B27 and ankylosing spondylitis; CD21 as the EBV receptor) and 13 (syphilis reverse algorithm), and Traps 5 (multiplex bead vs ELISA autoantibody results) and 6 (cytokines in blood). Checked against Braun 2023, Sugano 1997, the CDC 2024 syphilis laboratory recommendations (Papp 2024), Ortiz 2020, Bauer 2023, Zaminski 2023, Satoh 2015, Liu 2021 and Trajman 2013, all read as Europe PMC full text. Trap 5’s dodge that multiplex bead assays “detect high-avidity antibodies only” is contradicted by Zaminski 2023, which states enzyme immunoassays including the multiplex flow immunoassay detect low- and high-avidity antibodies, while Bauer 2023 assigns high-avidity detection to the Farr assay (register flag rv-multiplex-high-avidity-only). Trap 6’s “rarely reach measurable blood concentrations” and “investigational, not routine” are not taught as stated: Liu 2021 describes trace levels and pre-analytical problems but also clinical uses of cytokine levels (register flag rv-cytokine-blood-levels-context). The reverse algorithm is taught from US CDC guidance (register flag rv-syphilis-reverse-us-guideline). Not taught: other HLA disease associations, EBV serology, syphilis treatment and neurosyphilis.

objectives: Explain why HLA-B27 is a risk marker for ankylosing spondylitis and not a screening test, and name CD21 as the B-cell receptor that EBV uses.
Interpret the steps and discordant result of the reverse syphilis screening algorithm.
Explain why anti-dsDNA results differ between methods and why cytokines are hard to measure reliably in blood.

scenes.title: Three results, three overreadings
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three results reach the immunology bench — (1) a 24-year-old blood donor with no symptoms whose HLA-B27 typing is positive; (2) a pregnant patient whose automated treponemal screen is reactive but whose reflex RPR is nonreactive; (3) a patient with lupus whose anti-dsDNA is positive on one platform and negative on another the same day. A note asks for serum cytokine levels to monitor the lupus. Question token: “Disease, false positive, or a method limit?”

cues.text: Three results arrive. A healthy twenty-four-year-old blood donor types positive for HLA-B27.
A pregnant patient has a reactive treponemal screen but a nonreactive RPR. And a lupus patient is anti-dsDNA positive on one platform and negative on another, on the same day.
Is that ankylosing spondylitis, a false positive, and a lab error? Or is each result showing the limits of its method?

props.label: Disease, false positive, or a method limit?

scenes.title: What each marker really is
scenes.altText: Schematic cards. HLA-B27: an HLA class I molecule that presents peptides to CD8+ T cells; carried by about 8% of mid-Europeans; about 60–90% of axial spondyloarthritis patients carry it, but only about 1–2% of B27-positive people develop ankylosing spondylitis in a lifetime; not a screening test for people without symptoms. CD21: complement receptor 2 (CR2), the receptor for C3dg on B cells; EBV glycoprotein gp350/220 binds it, which is how EBV enters normal B cells. Treponemal tests detect antibodies to Treponema pallidum antigens and usually stay reactive for life; nontreponemal (lipoidal antigen) tests such as RPR give a titre that usually falls at least fourfold within 12 months of treatment.

cues.text: HLA-B27 is an HLA class one molecule that presents peptides to CD8 T cells. About sixty to ninety percent of people with axial spondyloarthritis carry it.
But about eight percent of mid-Europeans carry B27, and only one to two percent of carriers develop ankylosing spondylitis. So B27 cannot screen people without symptoms.
CD21, complement receptor two, is the B-cell receptor for the complement fragment C3dg. Epstein-Barr virus binds it with its envelope glycoprotein gp350, which is how the virus infects B cells.

Syphilis has two antibody families. Treponemal antibodies usually stay for life. Nontreponemal antibodies, measured by RPR, give a titre that usually falls at least fourfold within a year of treatment.

scenes.title: The reverse syphilis algorithm
scenes.altText: Flow diagram (CDC 2024): reverse algorithm starts with an automated treponemal immunoassay (EIA or CIA). Nonreactive → no serologic evidence of syphilis. Reactive → must be followed by a quantitative nontreponemal test (RPR) reported with an endpoint titre. RPR reactive → syphilis, current or past; the titre, history and examination classify the stage and set the baseline for follow-up. RPR nonreactive → discordant → second treponemal test with a different format and different antigens, such as TPPA (the preferred manual treponemal test). Second treponemal reactive → treponemal antibodies confirmed; cannot separate previously treated from untreated infection, so history decides. Second treponemal nonreactive → initial screen counted as a false positive. Side note: traditional and reverse algorithms are both acceptable and agree about 99%; the reverse algorithm may detect more early syphilis but may give more false positives in low-prevalence populations.

cues.text: The reverse algorithm starts with an automated treponemal immunoassay. If it is reactive, the CDC says it must be followed by a quantitative nontreponemal test, such as an RPR with an endpoint titre.
A reactive RPR means syphilis, current or past. The titre, the history and the examination help classify the stage, and the titre is the baseline for following treatment.

A nonreactive RPR is discordant. It is settled by a second treponemal test with a different format and different antigens, such as TPPA. Reactive: the antibodies are real, but the test cannot tell treated from untreated infection. Nonreactive: the first screen was a false positive.
Both algorithms are acceptable and agree about ninety-nine percent of the time. Starting treponemal may catch more early syphilis, but gives more false positives when syphilis is rare.

props.label: Both algorithms OK · ~99% agree · reverse: more early cases, more false +

scenes.title: When methods disagree
scenes.altText: Left card: anti-dsDNA methods. The Farr radioimmunoassay detects high-avidity antibodies; the Crithidia luciliae immunofluorescence test (CLIFT) detects medium- to high-avidity antibodies; enzyme immunoassays, including the multiplex flow (bead) immunoassay, detect low- and high-avidity antibodies. In one SLE cohort, 36% of paired multiplex EIA and CLIFT results disagreed; bead assays and ELISA also differ significantly for anti-dsDNA, Sm and La. Right card: cytokines in blood circulate in trace (picomolar) amounts, are secreted in brief bursts, have short half-lives, can bind soluble receptors that immunoassays may not recognise, and change with handling, storage and freeze-thaw. Token: the interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) measures IFN-γ released by the patient’s T cells after stimulation with M. tuberculosis antigens (ESAT-6, CFP-10, TB7.7). Hook answers card.

cues.text: Anti-dsDNA methods do not see the same antibodies. The Farr assay detects high-avidity antibodies. Enzyme immunoassays, including multiplex bead assays, detect low and high avidity.
In one lupus cohort, a third of paired multiplex and Crithidia results disagreed, and bead assays differ from ELISA for anti-dsDNA too. Discordance is expected, not an error.

Cytokines are harder still. They circulate in trace amounts, in short bursts, with short half-lives. Some bind soluble receptors that immunoassays miss, and levels shift with handling and freeze-thaw. The interferon-gamma release assay works because it stimulates the patient’s T cells with tuberculosis antigens and measures the interferon they release.

Back to the hook. The donor’s B27 is a risk marker, not a diagnosis. The pregnant patient needs a second treponemal test such as TPPA. And the lupus patient’s two results reflect two methods, so trend one method over time.

props.label: IGRA: stimulate T cells, measure IFN-γ

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “HLA-B27 positive = ankylosing spondylitis” (✓ only about 1–2% of carriers develop AS; B27 cannot screen people without symptoms); “Reactive treponemal screen with nonreactive RPR = false positive” (✓ settle it with a second treponemal test of a different format, such as TPPA); “A multiplex bead assay and an ELISA should give the same anti-dsDNA result” (✓ methods differ in antigen and avidity; discordance is common).

cues.text: Trap one: HLA-B27 positive means ankylosing spondylitis. No: only one to two percent of carriers develop it, so B27 cannot screen healthy people.
Trap two: a reactive treponemal screen with a nonreactive RPR is a false positive. Not yet: a second treponemal test of a different format, such as TPPA, decides.
Trap three: a bead assay and an ELISA should agree on anti-dsDNA. No: they use different antigens and catch different avidities, and disagreement is common.

props.title: ✗ “Bead and ELISA anti-dsDNA must match.”
lines: ✓ Different antigens and avidity; discordance common

scenes.title: Ticket, tattoo, thermometer
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “HLA-B27 is a TICKET, not the trip. Treponemal antibodies are a TATTOO that stays; the RPR titre is a THERMOMETER that rises and falls. Two anti-dsDNA assays are two NETS with different mesh. Cytokines are WHISPERS — faint and brief.” Tokens: ticket = B27 · tattoo = treponemal · thermometer = RPR · nets = assays. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: HLA-B27 is a ticket, not the trip. Treponemal antibodies are a tattoo that stays. The RPR titre is a thermometer that rises and falls. Two anti-dsDNA assays are nets with different mesh. And cytokines are whispers: faint and brief.

Where it breaks: about fifteen to twenty-five percent of people treated for primary syphilis lose the treponemal tattoo within two to three years; the RPR thermometer can read high for reasons other than syphilis; avidity is only one reason assays differ; and the IGRA does measure a cytokine, after stimulating cells in the tube.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Avidity is one reason of several
IGRA measures a cytokine after stimulation

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “B27 = risk, not diagnosis · treponemal + → quantitative RPR → discordant → TPPA”, “Anti-dsDNA methods differ · blood cytokines are faint and fragile”.

cues.text: Read each immune result for what its method can show, because HLA-B27 marks risk rather than disease, a reactive treponemal screen needs a quantitative RPR and a second treponemal test when they disagree, and anti-dsDNA platforms and blood cytokine levels can differ for purely technical reasons.

props.label: B27 = risk · treponemal + → RPR titre → discordant → TPPA
Anti-dsDNA methods differ · blood cytokines: faint, brief, fragile

explanation.what: Plain language: some lab results are easy to overread. HLA-B27 is an inherited tissue type that raises the chance of a spine disease but does not prove it. EBV gets into B cells by docking on a surface protein called CD21. In syphilis, one antibody type stays for life and another rises and falls with active infection, so labs use both. Different anti-DNA tests catch different antibodies, and cytokines in blood are faint, short-lived and easily disturbed. Scientific terms: HLA class I, HLA-B27, axial spondyloarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis (AS), CD21 (complement receptor 2, CR2), C3dg, gp350/220, treponemal immunoassay (EIA, CIA), nontreponemal (lipoidal antigen) test, rapid plasma reagin (RPR), endpoint titre, Treponema pallidum particle agglutination (TPPA), reverse sequence algorithm, Farr radioimmunoassay, Crithidia luciliae immunofluorescence test (CLIFT), multiplex flow (bead) immunoassay, avidity, soluble cytokine receptors, interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA).
explanation.why: HLA-B27 presents peptides to CD8 T cells and accounts for only part of the genetic risk of AS, so most carriers stay well. EBV glycoprotein gp350/220 mimics the C3dg binding site on CD21. Treponemal antibodies usually persist after treatment, while nontreponemal titres track infection status and treatment response, so the two are combined. Assays with different antigens and avidity windows catch different antibody populations. Cytokines exist in picomolar amounts with short half-lives and may be bound by soluble receptors.
explanation.measure: HLA-B27: about 8% of mid-Europeans; about 60–90% of axSpA patients; lifetime AS risk of a B27 carrier about 1–2%. Reverse algorithm: treponemal immunoassay → if reactive, quantitative nontreponemal test with endpoint titre → if nonreactive, second treponemal test of a different format and antigens (e.g. TPPA). Nontreponemal titres usually fall at least fourfold within 12 months of treatment; a fourfold change on the same test is significant. Anti-dsDNA: 36% of paired multiplex EIA and CLIFT results discordant in one cohort. Cytokines: minimise freeze-thaw; most are stable for up to three cycles. IGRA: IFN-γ released after stimulation with ESAT-6, CFP-10 (and TB7.7 in QuantiFERON).
explanation.differs: Risk allele (B27) vs disease (AS); treponemal (persists for life) vs nontreponemal (titre falls after treatment); traditional (nontreponemal first) vs reverse (treponemal first) algorithm; Farr (high avidity) vs EIA and bead assays (low and high avidity); circulating cytokine levels vs stimulated release in an IGRA.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: pick the next step after a reactive treponemal screen and nonreactive RPR; recognise that a positive B27 in a healthy person does not mean AS; name CD21 as the EBV receptor; explain why two anti-dsDNA methods disagree; identify a reason cytokine levels in blood are unreliable.

comparisons.title: Treponemal vs nontreponemal tests

left.label: Treponemal
points: Usually reactive for life; cannot monitor therapy

right.label: Nontreponemal (RPR)
points: Falls at least fourfold after treatment; biologic false positives

comparisons.distinguisher: Persistence vs a titre that rises and falls; both are needed to classify a patient.

comparisons.title: Anti-dsDNA: Farr vs EIA and bead assays
comparisons.distinguisher: Which avidity window and antigen the method captures; results are not interchangeable.

mnemonic.text: HLA-B27 is a TICKET, not the trip. Treponemal antibodies are a TATTOO that stays; the RPR titre is a THERMOMETER that rises and falls. Two anti-dsDNA assays are two NETS with different mesh. Cytokines are WHISPERS: faint and brief.
mnemonic.explanation: Separates risk from disease, lifelong from activity-linked antibodies, and method limits from true disagreement.
mnemonic.limitation: About 15–25% of people treated for primary syphilis revert to a nonreactive treponemal test within 2–3 years; RPR has biologic false positives; avidity is only one reason assays differ; the IGRA does measure a cytokine, after stimulating cells.

analogyLimitations: Algorithm and assay drawings are schematic.
Percentages come from single reviews or cohorts and vary by population and method.
takeaway: Read each immune result for what its method can show, because HLA-B27 marks risk rather than disease, a reactive treponemal screen needs a quantitative RPR and a second treponemal test when they disagree, and anti-dsDNA platforms and blood cytokine levels can differ for purely technical reasons.

questions.stem: A laboratory uses the reverse syphilis algorithm. A pregnant patient has a reactive treponemal chemiluminescence immunoassay and a nonreactive quantitative RPR. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: A second treponemal test with a different format and antigens, such as TPPA
options.rationale: Correct. The CDC recommends adjudicating discordant reverse-algorithm results with a second treponemal assay of a different format, such as TPPA.

options.text: Report the screen as a false positive
options.rationale: Incorrect. A false positive is defined only when the second treponemal test is also nonreactive.
Incorrect. Repeating the same assay does not resolve the discordance; a different format and antigens are needed.
Incorrect. Treponemal antibodies cannot separate current from previously treated infection, and the RPR is nonreactive.

questions.stem: A healthy blood donor with no back pain is found to be HLA-B27 positive. Which statement is best supported?

options.text: Most B27 carriers never develop ankylosing spondylitis
options.rationale: Correct. The lifetime chance of a B27-positive person developing AS is only about 1–2%.
Incorrect. B27 is a risk allele, and testing cannot be used to screen people without symptoms.

options.text: HLA-B27 is an HLA class II molecule
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-B27 belongs to the HLA class I family and presents peptides to CD8 T cells.

options.text: B27 explains nearly all of the genetic risk of AS
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-B27 accounts for about a quarter of the heritability; many other loci contribute.

questions.stem: Which feature makes cytokine levels in blood difficult to measure reliably?

options.text: Trace concentrations and short half-lives, with binding to soluble receptors
options.rationale: Correct. Cytokines circulate in picomolar amounts, have short half-lives, and some bound forms may not be recognised by immunoassays.

options.text: Cytokines are stable for weeks at room temperature
options.rationale: Incorrect. Cytokines can degrade during collection and processing, so careful handling is essential.

options.text: Cytokines cannot be measured by any immunoassay
options.rationale: Incorrect. ELISA is one of the most commonly used methods for cytokine quantification.

options.text: Repeated freeze-thaw cycles never affect cytokine levels
options.rationale: Incorrect. Levels can rise or fall with repeated freeze-thaw, so samples should undergo minimal freeze-thawing.

claims.text: HLA-B27 is class I; prevalence about 8%; 60–90% of axSpA carry it; about 25% of heritability; 1–2% lifetime AS risk in carriers; not a screening test.
CD21 (CR2) is the C3dg receptor on B cells and the EBV receptor via gp350/220.

Reverse algorithm steps, quantitative RPR follow-up, discordant adjudication with a second treponemal test (e.g. TPPA), false-positive definition, treponemal persistence and seroreversion, fourfold titre decline, ~99% concurrence, early detection and low-prevalence false positives.
Farr detects high-avidity anti-dsDNA; CLIFT medium-high; EIA including multiplex bead detects low and high; 36% paired discordance; bead vs ELISA differences.
Cytokines in trace amounts with short half-lives; soluble receptors; handling and freeze-thaw effects; IGRA measures IFN-γ after antigen stimulation.
Reviewer’s statements that multiplex bead assays detect high-avidity antibodies only and that high-avidity anti-dsDNA tracks real disease activity.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 44 Trap 5 says multiplex bead assays detect high-avidity antibodies only, so they track the Farr assay and disease activity. Zaminski 2023 states enzyme immunoassays, including the multiplex flow immunoassay, detect low- and high-avidity antibodies, and Bauer 2023 assigns particular high-avidity detection to the Farr assay and calls the anti-dsDNA–activity link controversial. The lesson teaches that methods differ in antigen and avidity and that discordance is common (register flag rv-multiplex-high-avidity-only).

Ch. 44 Trap 6 says cytokines rarely reach measurable blood concentrations and are investigational, not routine. Liu 2021 supports trace (pM) levels, short half-lives, soluble-receptor binding and handling effects that make measurement difficult, but also describes clinical use of cytokine levels to monitor immune status and cytokine storm. Routine-use status was not verified (register flag rv-cytokine-blood-levels-context).
The reverse algorithm steps are taught from US CDC 2024 laboratory recommendations (Papp 2024). Philippine guidance was not checked and may differ (register flag rv-syphilis-reverse-us-guideline).
